questions.q: Two numbers 3 and 15 have HCF 3 with coprime multipliers 1 and 5. Verify by computing hcf = 3 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 3 and 15 given their HCF is 3 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 3 and 15 is 15. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 3 cm and 15 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 3 minutes and 15 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 36 are there up to 100?
For the digits 1, 2, 3, 3 form the largest and smallest 4-digit numbers and find their difference (Kaprekar step).
The number 5619 is split into landmark groups of 1000, 100 and 10. How many complete 1000-groups does it contain?
Find the digit sum of 5619.
Find the remainder when the digit sum of 5619 (= 21) is divided by 9.
Take the 2-digit number 73, reverse its digits to get 37, and find the positive difference (a Kaprekar-style step).
For the 2-digit number 73 (digits 7 and 3), the difference between the number and its reversal is always 9 x (difference of digits). Compute that difference.

solution_steps.explain: verify the number-theory claim numerically: lhs = 3 ** 3 + 4 ** 3 gives 91
verify the number-theory claim numerically: diff = 5 ** 3 - lhs gives 34

questions.q: Fermat's Last Theorem says x^n + y^n = z^n has no positive solutions for n > 2. For n = 3 compute 5^3 - (3^3 + 4^3) to see it is not zero.
Check whether 6 is a perfect number: its proper divisors are 1, 2 and 3. Find their sum.
The numbers 11 and 13 are consecutive primes. How far apart are they (twin primes differ by 2)?
Are 8 and 15 co-prime? Their common factors are only 1, so their HCF is what?
Divisibility by 9: a number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is. Find the digit sum of 729 and report the digit sum.
Divisibility by 11: add and subtract alternate digits of 2728 from the right (8 - 2 + 7 - 2) and report the result.

Find the LCM of 56 and 64 given their HCF is 8 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 56 and 64 is 448. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 56 cm and 64 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 56 minutes and 64 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 24 are there up to 96?

Find the LCM of 35 and 7 given their HCF is 7 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 35 and 7 is 35. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 35 cm and 7 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 35 minutes and 7 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 30 are there up to 90?
Two numbers 60 and 12 have HCF 12 with coprime multipliers 5 and 1. Verify by computing hcf = 12 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 60 and 12 given their HCF is 12 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 60 and 12 is 60. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 60 cm and 12 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 60 minutes and 12 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 36 are there up to 96?
